Simulate Markov Chain Trajectories

Source: R/02_sim.R
sim.Rd

Generate one or more independent sample paths from a finite-state, time-homogeneous Markov chain.

Usage

sim(m, x, n = 1)

Arguments

m

A single positive integer giving the number of observations per trajectory, including the initial state.

x

A MarkovChain object.

n

A single positive integer giving the number of trajectories.

Value

If n = 1, an ordered factor of length m with one level per state in chain order. If n > 1, an n by m character matrix of state labels, with one trajectory per row and observations in time order across columns. Pass a matrix with at least two columns directly to fit() to pool its within-trajectory transitions.

Details

Each trajectory starts with a fresh draw from the initial distribution x$a. Each subsequent state is drawn from the row of x$P for the current state. Simulating multiple paths with a fixed random seed gives the same draws as successive single-path calls with that seed.

See also

MarkovChain(), fit(), stat()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(a = c(0.5, 0.5), P = P)
set.seed(1)
sim(m = 5, x = x)
#> [1] 2 2 2 1 1
#> Levels: 1 < 2
paths <- sim(m = 20, x = x, n = 10)
fit(paths)
#> Markov Chain
#>   Number of states: 2 
#> 
#>   Initial distribution (a):
#>       1   2 
#>     0.2 0.8 
#> 
#>   Transition matrix (P):
#>               1         2
#>     1 0.7634409 0.2365591
#>     2 0.2783505 0.7216495
